observedBehaviour: PathBuilder's coordinates are normalized to the shape's own box, from 0 to 1, with the origin at the BOTTOM-LEFT and y increasing upward - the opposite of the page's reading direction and of every other measurement in this workflow. Nothing in the signatures says so: moveTo(double x, double y) reads as points, and the allow-list carries no units. Passing point values does not fail and does not fill the box either; it draws a DIFFERENT shape, silently. Measured: one triangle described normalized covers 0.25 of its box, which is its true area, and the same triangle described in points covers 0.13. That is why the mistake surfaces as a curved band rendering flat rather than as an error anyone can search for. Control points may overshoot 0..1 on purpose; that is what lets a curve bulge past its box.

minimalReproduction.arrangement: The same triangle described twice - once in normalized coordinates and once in points - each rendered alone and rasterised, with a third render placing a 0..0.25 square in a corner to locate the origin. The two descriptions covering different areas is the finding; the normalized one matching the triangle's true area says which of the two the builder reads.

workaround: Divide by the shape's own size before calling: a band PAGE_W wide and BAND_H tall whose right edge stops BAND_H_RIGHT below the page top is lineTo(1, (BAND_H - BAND_H_RIGHT) / BAND_H), not lineTo(PAGE_W, BAND_H_RIGHT). Keep the geometry in points in named constants and normalize at the call, so the arithmetic stays readable and the derivation survives a size change.

sourceRun.note: The invoice's curved header band rendered as a flat rectangle on the first pass. The answer was in GraphCompose's own VectorPathExample Javadoc and in neither the allow-list nor the skill pack, which is the gap this observation closes until the pack carries it.
